html:
SMTO-CFG-0039 — SMTO's settings file has an empty model API key

GUID: ef3ea62a-6987-4c5f-9ace-41e14c395d30
Slug: config-llm-api-key-is-required
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO's startup settings file (usually config.yaml) has an api_key line for the AI model with nothing in it, so SMTO stopped. The key works like a password for connecting to the model service.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file (usually config.yaml) in a plain text editor and find api_key under the llm section. That is the line SMTO found empty.
  2. Delete the empty api_key line, save the file, and start SMTO again. Without the line, SMTO uses a stand-in value and can start; a line with nothing in it is refused.
  3. If your model service needs a key, once SMTO is running open Settings › Setup › Model routing, type the key into the Main connection's API key box, and select Save Main. SMTO keeps keys entered there in its protected credential store instead of in a plain text file.
  4. If someone else manages SMTO's settings, send them this message and let them enter the key themselves. An API key works like a password; keeping it out of messages and screenshots stops it from leaking.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the message from the window where SMTO was started) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Never paste the API key into a conversation, a screenshot or an error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Configuration validation failed because the effective model-provider API key (llm.api_key in the bootstrap YAML, or Settings.llm_api_key) is blank after trimming.

What this means

  • Effective model-provider api_key is empty after configuration normalization. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Effective model-provider api_key is empty after configuration normalization.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the owning provider credential setting privately; this local presence check does not prove whether a supplied key is accepted remotely.

How to fix it

  • Remove the blank llm.api_key from the bootstrap YAML to use the default placeholder ("local"), or set it to a non-blank value; Settings applies the same check to llm_api_key, including values from the managed settings overrides. Prefer storing provider credentials through the Model routing connection's API key field, and keep them out of task text, command arguments and reports; confirm access separately against the provider.
  • Configure the intended model provider credential through the supported secret setting. Do not paste the key into task prompts or error reports.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A configured private value passes local validation and separate provider authentication confirms intended access.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
